exposure: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet syndrome (HELLP)
cohort: Three individuals (a 24-year-old male, a 19-year-old male, and a 28-year-old postpartum female) diagnosed with hepatic infarcts of the native liver were identified from 1865 consecutive adult and pediatric autopsies.
finding: Hepatic infarcts are rare vascular lesions of the nontransplant liver that can be caused by uncommon factors such as hornet stings, acute pancreatitis, and HELLP syndrome, and may present with microthrombi even in the absence of macroscopic thrombi.
